text:
David: quick follow-up from the RFC review — we need a minimal set of invariants that must hold across hosted / dedicated / private. proposing a "policy escrow" pattern: control plane holds an encrypted policy token + release predicate. runtime must attest before token is released. thoughts?
Lina: +1 on invariants. can we make the escrow release predicate pluggable? some private installs will want KMS-based release vs hosted attestation.
Sam: curious about failure modes. if a private deployment is air-gapped and attestation fails, do we fail closed (deny) or fail open (serve with limited features)?
Kate: for enterprise customers, fail-closed is usually required for policy-sensitive checks. but we also need a safety-net to avoid outage for low-risk requests. maybe graded enforcement levels: audit-only, warn, enforce.
David: exactly — graded enforcement. default for hosted = enforce, dedicated = warn/enforce depending on contract, private = customer-configurable.
Lina: operational concern: how to prove attestation? hardware-backed attestation (SGX/TPM) is ideal but not universal. maybe allow both signed lease from runtime agent OR mTLS + signed runtime nonce from controlplane.
Sam: encryption key lifecycle is hairy. if control plane holds the escrowed token, we need clear rotation semantics and audit trail (who requested release, when). also minimize plaintext lifetime on runtime.
Kate: for private installs, we can support KMS integration: control plane stores ciphertext but customers manage keys. release predicate becomes "customer-authorize" which the local operator triggers. no control-plane network roundtrip required.
David: nice. that covers offline. for hosted/dedicated, release flow could be: runtime requests nonce -> controlplane issues challenge -> runtime signs with attestor -> controlplane verifies -> releases token (short-lived).
Lina: add TTL on released tokens (e.g., 5m) and require continuous keepalives for long-lived sessions. reduces blast radius if leaked.
Sam: also think about audit ingestion. release events must be replicated to telemetry with hashes (not plaintext). need correlation IDs for postmortem.
Kate: policy definition language: keep small. constraints should be boolean predicates over signals (tenant, model, route, time, legal-region). avoid Turing-complete policies.
David: agreed. smaller DSL makes verification simpler. we should also define a compatibility matrix: which signals are available in each hosting mode (hosted has full signals, dedicated subset, private depends on operator config).
Lina: propose a simple API surface for runtime to ask "is_enforced(policy_id, context)" which returns {decision, evidence, release_token?}. evidence = signed attestation or audit-hash.
Sam: one more tradeoff: latency. attestation roundtrip adds ~20-100ms. for tight latency SLOs we should cache release_token per route/batch to amortize. cache invalidation tied to model/version rollouts.
David: notes for RFC update: 1) define invariants list 2) spec policy escrow flow + primitives (challenge, attestation types, token format, TTL) 3) define enforcement levels and default mapping by hosting mode 4) define signals compatibility matrix 5) telemetry + audit contract 6) KMS/offline escrow option for private installs.
Kate: ops playbook additions: how to debug escrow failures (check attestor logs, verify time skew, inspect audit hashes). also add a fallback policy for emergency operator override (requires 2-person approval).
Lina: will draft a lightweight sequence diagram and sample config snippet:
```
policy_escrow:
  id: data_exfil_prevention_v1
  mode: attest
  release_predicate: signed_attestation
  ttl: 300 # seconds
  enforcement: enforce
```
David: thanks — next steps: Lina drafts diagram & sample, Sam drafts audit schema, Kate drafts playbook, I'll wire these into the RFC and schedule a follow-up next week.
